Commentary.Commentary: Right then! That is all we have from this match. The hosts have gone 4-0 up and they will be looking for a whitewash come the final ODI. It might be a dead rubber but India Women will be looking to get one win in order to take some momentum with them into the World Cup. The final match of this tour will be played on Thursday, the 24th of February. The first ball will be bowled at 0330 IST (2200 GMT, previous day) but the coverage will begin much sooner. Do join us then. Take care and goodbye!

New Zealand Women skipper, Sophie Devine says with the bat they showed great intent. Adds, they know they can save a few more runs with better fielding and would work on it. Adds, the fans are backing us and she is glad they have the backing with the World Cup coming up.

Mithali Raj, the India Women captain is in for a chat. She says, they have been trying to work out on some combination and feels that the bowlers need to be more consistent and they will be looking to improve that department. Mentions, Richa Ghosh is a very exciting player for India.

Amelia Kerr is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for yet another impressive outing with both the bat as well as the ball. She says, the openers got off to a flier and she is glad she could carry on the good work. Adds that she has worked a lot on herself in the winter and is all prepped up for a huge summer season. Mentions, to have such confidence heading into the World Cup is a massive advantage.
Presentation ceremony...

A daunting task was made almost impossible when Shafali Verma and Yastika Bhatia were sent packing early, neither of them even troubling the scorers. Smriti Mandhana came back into the side and played a few shots but she too perished soon. It was then a counter-attacking partnership from the skipper, Mithali Raj and young pocket-sized dynamite Richa Ghosh worth 82-runs which brought belief back into the Indian camp. Ghosh got out after reaching the 50-run mark and Raj followed suit as she looked to up the ante. After that, it was just a question of when the innings ends and by how much the hosts would win. The tail was cleaned up by Amelia Kerr and the visitors were handed a thumping defeat. They will now look to get something out of this series before the World Cup starts and would want to win the final match of the tour.

New Zealand Women have now gone 4-0 up in the five-match series and it was a dominating display with both the bat and the ball today from the hosts. To be honest, the win was set up with the bat, when the hosts scored 191. But just to seal the deal, Frances Mackay and Jess Kerr picked up early wickets to nip the chase in the bud in the Powerplay itself They had the visitors 19 for 4 inside 5 overs and it was a stern resistance then from Ghosh and Raj that delayed the win. Once those two were dismissed in successive overs, the hosts cleaned up the tail in almost no time. Mackay and Jess Kerr ended with two wickets each but Hayley Jensen and Amelia Kerr were the ones who did the job at the top and at the death respectively. Amelia Kerr rounded off a dominant all-around performance with 3 wickets in her final over. New Zealand Women will be pleased with that showing.

OUT! CLEANED UP! Three wickets in the over to end the innings of India Women. Amelia Kerr shining with the ball as well. A googly, full and on the stumps. Rajeshwari Gayakwad clears her front leg and tries to heave it across the line but misses. The ball goes through to shatter the stumps. New Zealand Women win the game by 63 runs.
FOUR! Nicely played. Too full, angled down leg. Rajeshwari Gayakwad glances it down to fine leg for a boundary.
Full and on off, blocked out solidly.
Rajeshwari Gayakwad is the last batter in for India and she will also face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! Cleaned up! A team Hat-Trick! Amelia Kerr has two in two and Renuka Singh is out for a golden duck. This is a peach of a delivery. It's the wrong 'un, nicely tossed up and around off. Renuka Singh presses forward to defend but the ball turns in sharply and goes through the gap between bat and pad, crashing int0o middle stump. New Zealand Women now just one wicket away from winning the match and Kerr is on a hat-trick. Is there anything this woman can't do?
Renuka Singh comes in to bat now.

OUT! TIMBER! Floated, full and on the stumps. Deepti Sharma shuffles across and looks to sweep it away but misses it completely. The ball sneaks behind her and shatters the stumps. New Zealand Women look to be in a hurry to end things here.
Meghna Singh walks in at number 9.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one holes out for India. Frances Mackay gets some extra bounce off the deck this time. It is flighted, full and on off. Sneh Rana looks to sweep it away. The ball flies off the top edge and goes towards short fine leg and Rosemary Mair takes a dolly.
Commentary.Howout: c Rosemary Mair b Frances Mackay

Commentary.Commentary: LEG BYE! Floated, full and on the pads. Sharma looks to sweep it away but misses. The ball brushes her pads and rolls towards square leg. They collect a leg bye.
Tossed up, on off. Rana pushes it to cover for one.
Quicker, flatter and outside off. Rana steers it down to third man for a couple now.
Fuller and on the pads. Sharma tucks it to square leg for one.
Flatter and outside off. Sharma guides it down to third man for a brace.
Frances Mackay (2-0-16-1) comes back in to replace Rosemary Mair.
Short and on the stumps. Rana goes back and looks to cut it away. She gets it out off her inner half.
Fuller and on the pads. Rana glances it to fine leg for a brace.
Short and on off. Sharma pulls it to deep mid-wicket for one more.
Full and on off. Rana pushes it to cover for one.

What a chance this was! Martin misses out on a stumping opportunity behind the stumps. Tossed up, full and outside off. Rana comes down the track only to get beaten on the inside edge. The keeper fails to collect the ball and Rana gets enough time to get back to safety.
Short and on off. Rana pushes it to cover.
WIDE! Flatter, down leg. Rana misses her flick. Wide called.
Amelia Kerr (2-0-21-0) is back into the attack.
A short ball, on off. Rana drags her pull to square leg for a single.
Length ball, outside off. Rana looks to chase it but misses.
Back of a length, outside off. Sharma works it to covers for one.
A length ball, on the pads. Deepti Sharma flicks it to fine leg for a brace.
Back of a length, on off. Sneh Rana pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
WIDE! Length ball, wide outside off. Sneh Rana looks to chase it but misses. Wide called.
A length ball, on off. Rana pushes it to cover. The fielder does well to get low to her right and stop the ball.
A length ball, around middle. Rana stays in her crease and just turns it on the leg side for a single.
On off, this is pushed out towards covers.
Sneh Rana comes in to bat now.

OUT! Cleaned up! Mithali Raj perishes and that should be the game for New Zealand Women. This is smart bowling from Jess Kerr. She knew that Raj was looking to charge down the track and muscle it leg side. Kerr bowls it slower and pulls back her length a bit as well. Raj does charge down the track but is completely undone by the lack of pace. The ball hits the top of off stump and the Indian skipper has to depart.
Length again, close to the off stump. Deepti Sharma cuts it really late towards short third man for a run.
On off, Raj hangs back and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and leg, this is flicked towards mid-wicket for a quick single.
SIX! Sweetly timed! Pitched up, on middle. Mithali Raj swings freely and manages to clear the wide long on fence with ease.
Deepti Sharma is the new batter in.

OUT! TAKEN! That is a brilliant catch from Amelia Kerr and the dangerous Richa Ghosh is a goner! Hayley Jensen hits the length hard and angles it at the body. The length is neither too full or too short and Ghosh opts to go big. She lifts it off the splice of the bat and the ball is skied towards the cow corner fence. Amelia Kerr runs in from the mid-wicket fence and slides in to take a really good catch. End of an entertaining innings from young Richa Ghosh.
Commentary.Howout: c Amelia Kerr b Hayley Jensen

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and outside off. Richa Ghosh dances down the track and carves it over the point region. The ball slows up and the fielder from deep cover is able to cut it off. The batters get a couple of runs.

This is excellent bowling! Jensen sees Raj making room and follows her with a fuller delivery. Raj looks to heave it leg side but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball goes towards point and they sneak in a single as well.
Leg bye! This is slower and down the leg side. Ghosh misses the flick and gets it off her pads towards leg slip. The keeper dives to make a stop but the batters to get a leg bye.
Full and angling into leg. Raj backs away and heaves it straight to mid-wicket for a quick single.
Back of a length, on off. Mithali Raj pulls it down to deep mid-wicket for just a single. Only 3 runs came off that over, a good one for New Zealand Women.
This is pushed wider. Raj tries to go big over extra cover but misses the ball completely.
Fifty for Richa Ghosh! The fastest ODI fifty for India Women as well. Shorter and around the hips. Ghosh pulls it down to fine leg for a single. Can Ghosh now pull off a miracle here?
Well bowled! A yorker, outside off. Ghosh jams it out.
Around off, this is pushed towards cover.
Leg bye! A length ball, around off. Raj looks to work it leg side but misses and gets hit on the pads. The ball goes onto the off side and they get a leg bye.
Sophie Devine comes on to bowl now.

SIX! Geez, that's a top shot! Fullish delivery, around off. Richa Ghosh makes a bit of room leg side and nonchalantly lifts it all the way over the wide long off fence for a biggie. She moves on to 49 now.
Nicely bowled! Slower and outside off. Ghosh looks to charge down the pitch and smoke it but only manages to get an inside edge back onto the pads.
Shorter in length, on off. Raj pulls it down to deep backward square leg for one.
FOUR! Mithali Raj looks to up the ante now and picks up a boundary. Pitched up, on middle. Raj heaves it over wide mid on and the ball races away into the fence.
On middle and leg, this is clipped towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

Leg bye! A length ball, angling in from around off. Mithali Raj goes right across her stumps to flick it away but misses. Raj gets hit on the pads and the ball rolls towards square leg. The bowler appeals but the umpire remains unmoved. They get a leg bye.
A slower bouncer, outside off. Richa Ghosh leaves it alone for the keeper.
SIX! KABOOM! Richa Ghosh is playing with fire. Full length, outside off. Richa Ghosh throws her blade at it and powers it over the cover fence.

Halt in play! Richa Ghosh gets hit right on the badge of the helmet. It was a spicy short ball from Mair and the physio is called out for a mandatory concussion check. Ghosh seems fine and play will now continue.

Back of a length, on middle. Richa Ghosh stays back and looks to pull it away but misses. The ball hits her on the helmet and lobs towards short third man. Rosemary Mair thinks it came off her gloves before it contacted with the helmet. But the umpires are not interested.
Full length, outside off. Richa Ghosh looks to chase it away but misses.
Full and on the stumps. Richa Ghosh scoops it over short fine leg for two runs.
Length and on off. Raj guides it to third man for one.
Rosemary Mair (1-0-12-0) comes back into the attack.
SIX! High and handsome! Floated, full and on off. Richa Ghosh gets low and slog-sweeps it over the mid-wicket fence.
On off, this is pushed to covers for one.
Length, on the pads. Richa Ghosh flicks it to fine leg for one.
Short and down leg. Ghosh makes room and looks to cut it away but misses.
On the pads, Raj clips it to mid-wicket for one run.
FOUR! Through the fielder! Short and outside off. Raj cuts it hard to point. The fielder get low but lets the ball go through her legs. Boundary.
SIX! HUGE! Floated, full, on middle and leg. Richa Ghosh clears her front leg and smokes it over the mid-wicket fence. Richa Ghosh is on a roll.
Short and outside off. Raj pulls it to mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, blocked out.
Angled into the pads. Raj comes down the track and looks to flick it away. It takes the leading edge and goes towards cover. Lands just short.
Flighted and on off. Richa Ghosh slams it down the ground for a single.
Floated and full, on off. Raj leans in and tries to scoop it away. It goes off the inside edge to fine leg for one.
Frances Mackay (1-0-7-1) is back on.
Short ball, on top of off. Richa Ghosh makes some room and looks to cut it away but misses it completely.
Flighted and full, on off. Richa Ghosh scoops it over the keeper's head for a brace.
Full and on off. Raj gets low on her knee and sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for another single.
Fuller, on leg. Ghosh comes down the track and clips it to mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! What a shot! Tossed up, full and on off. Richa Ghosh gets low and sweeps it to deep square leg for a booundary.
Fuller and on the stumps, blocked back to the bowler.
Amelia Kerr is into the attack now.
Length ball, on off. Raj defends it out solidly.
A slower bouncer, outside off. Ghosh looks to pull it away. It goes off the top edge towards fine leg. One taken.
FOUR! Richa Ghosh stepping on the gas now. Full length and on the stumps. Ghosh heaves it across the line through mid-wicket for another boundary.
FOUR! Up and over! Full length and outside off. Richa Ghosh lofts it over covers with good arm swing. The ball races away to the fence.
A short ball, outside off, with some extra bounce. Raj cuts it through backward point for a single.
Full length, outside off. Raj ends up splicing it over covers for a brace. Good running by the pair.
Good length, outside off, shaping away sharply. Richa Ghosh stays inside the crease and looks to cut it away but only manages to connect it with thin air.
WIDE! A sharp bouncer, shaping away. Richa Ghosh tries to cut it away but misses. Wide called.
FOUR! Into the gap! Richa Ghosh gets off the mark in some fine fashion. A short ball, on off. Richa Ghosh hangs back and pulls it through mid-wicket to bag a boundary.
Richa Ghosh comes in at number 6.

OUT! CAUGHT! Hayley Jensen gets her second wicket in no time. This is a brilliant catch to get rid of Smriti Mandhana. Back of a length, on off. Smriti Mandhana stays back and pulls it to deep square leg. Amelia Kerr runs to her right and dives in front to pouch the ball just above the grass. This is some exceptional fielding New Zealand Women players are showcasing here.
Commentary.Howout: c Amelia Kerr b Hayley Jensen

Commentary.Commentary: Full length, on off. Smriti Mandhana flicks it to mid-wicket. Not in the gap.
Fuller, on middle and leg. Raj flicks it through mid-wicket. She slips at the non-striker's end and they settle with one.
Good length, on off. Raj blocks it out solidly.
Back of a length, on the pads. Smriti Mandhana looks to heave it across the line but misses.
Length, on off, blocked out.
FOUR! Sweetly timed! Full length, on the pads. Smriti Mandhana leans in the shot, she uses her bottom hand and flicks it behind square on the leg side.
A short ball, on off. Raj stands back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
An inswinger, full and outside off. Mithali Raj drives it into covers.
Short ball, outside off. Smriti Mandhana taps it to point for a single.
A length ball, outside off, shaping away. Mithali Raj tries to hit it late and outside-edges it to the keeper but luckily it does not carry.
Mithali Raj comes in to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the fielder and Hayley Jensen now strikes in her first over! Pooja Vastrakar was expecting another short ball but Jensen pitches it right up and bowls it on middle. Vastrakar drives it on the up and the ball comes off the toe end of the bat. The ball goes straight towards Amy Satterthwaite at mid on and shes takes a dolly of a catch. India Women in a spot of bother here.
Commentary.Howout: c Amy Satterthwaite b Hayley Jensen

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely played! This is dug in short and Pooja Vastrakar manages to get on top of the bounce and pull it down to the square leg fence for a boundary.
Pitched up, on middle and Pooja Vastrakar with a lovely straight drive. Unfortunately for her, she hits it a bit too straight and the ball crashes into the stumps at the bowler's end.
This is shorter in length, around off. Vastrakar chops it towards cover.
Full, on middle and shaping away nicely. Pooja Vastrakar drives it straight towards mid on.
On a good length, around off. This is punched off the back foot towards cover.
Fullish delivery, angled across off and shaping away nicely. Mandhana leaves it alone.
Pooja Vastrakar is the new batter.

OUT! CAUGHT! Disaster for India! A golden duck here for Yastika Bhatia and Jess Kerr has an early wicket! This is banged in a bit short, around middle. Bhatia tries to pull it away when she is in no position to play that shot. Bhatia goes through the shot and the bat twists in her hand as she makes a connection with the ball. The ball pops up off the higher part of the bat and goes towards mid-wicket. It's Suzie Bates again who's under it and she takes it reverse-cup this time.
Commentary.Howout: c Suzie Bates b Jess Kerr

Commentary.Commentary: A length ball, outside off. Mandhana steps down the track and goes up and over point to pick up a single.
Good fielding! A tad short and wide, this is cutaway towards point where the fielder makes a brilliant stop.
Pitched up, on off and this is pushed towards mid off.
Yastika Bhatia comes in at number 3. Also, Jess Kerr to share the new ball.

OUT! TAKEN! What in the world happened here? Frances Mackay, the off spinner bowls a bumper, well outside off. How often do you even see that? Shafali Verma looks to take it on and sets up for the pull shot. Verma has to reach for it a bit and is through the shot early. The ball goes uppishly towards the mid-wicket region and Suzie Bates dives in front to take an excellent catch. Verma is out for a duck and New Zealand Women off to a perfect start.
Commentary.Howout: c Suzie Bates b Frances Mackay

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker and flatter, on middle. Verma punches it out towards mid on.
Top edge, but there's no one there. Sliding onto the pads, Mandhana looks to paddle it fine but gets a top edge. The ball lands safely around the short fine leg region and they get a single.
FOUR! Easily done! This is dragged down, outside off. Mandhana shuffles and pulls it behind square on the leg side for a boundary, the first of the innings.
Smriti Mandhana is up and running! Flatter, around off and this is squeezed through cover-point for a couple of runs.
Nicely tossed up, on a length and on middle. Smriti Mandhana gets pushed onto the back foot but manages to push it out.
